findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime pagination
findings.body: The optimized branch uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime', but OptimizedCursorPaginator implements numeric cursor key handling (math.floor/math.ceil on the field value and raw numeric values from cursors). AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime field, so building cursors will raise TypeError, and any cursor-based WHERE clause would compare the wrong type. Requests using optimized_pagination=true will fail.

findings.title: Negative offsets are passed to Django queryset slicing, which Django does not support
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows start_offset to be negative when enable_advanced_features is true and then executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing raises AssertionError for negative start/stop values; the comment claiming the ORM handles this is incorrect. This can turn invalid or crafted cursors into endpoint 500 errors.

findings.title: BasePaginator still permits negative offsets for previous cursors
findings.body: The new offset handling clamps negative offsets only when cursor.is_prev is false. For previous-page cursors, a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Since Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices, a malformed cursor can crash any endpoint using BasePaginator-derived paginators.

findings.title: Typo assigns queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by
findings.body: In build_queryset, when reversing an existing descending ordering for previous-page pagination, the code assigns queryset.query.order_b = tuple(new_order_by) instead of queryset.query.order_by. The ordering change is silently dropped, which can cause wrong ordering, duplicated rows, or skipped rows when paginating backwards over a queryset that already has descending ordering.

findings.title: Switching span buffer keys from sets to sorted sets without migration breaks existing Redis data
findings.body: process_spans now uses ZADD on span-buf:s:* keys, and add-buffer.lua uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE, but existing keys created by prior versions are Redis sets with the same key names. During rollout, operations on those existing set-type keys will fail with WRONGTYPE errors, causing span-buffer script failures and potential loss of in-flight spans. A new key namespace or drain/migration strategy is needed.

findings.title: Eviction limit is hardcoded in Lua and ignores SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans
findings.body: The Lua script caps segment buffers at 1000 members, while SpansBuffer still accepts max_segment_spans (default 1001) and no longer enforces it in Python. This makes the configuration option ineffective and creates a mismatch between the configured default and the actual enforced limit.

findings.title: Eviction can remove the root span while the has-root-span flag remains set
findings.body: zpopmin evicts the lowest-scored members by end_timestamp_precise. If the root/segment span is among the evicted members, the span-buf:hrs:* key may still indicate that the segment has a root span, causing the segment to be flushed under root-span timing while no flushed payload is marked is_segment. This can produce inconsistent or rootless segments.

findings.title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl as the segment_page_size constructor argument
findings.body: SpansBuffer.__reduce__ returns four positional constructor arguments: assigned_shards, span_buffer_timeout_secs, span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, and self.redis_ttl. The constructor's fourth positional parameter is segment_page_size; redis_ttl is the seventh parameter. When SpansBuffer is unpickled (for example, when used with multiprocessing), it will be restored with segment_page_size set to the TTL value and redis_ttl reset to its default.

findings.title: Direct access to end_timestamp_precise can crash the consumer on missing field
findings.body: process_batch reads val["end_timestamp_precise"] directly. If any incoming span message omits this field (for example, a legacy producer, malformed message, or schema evolution case), the consumer raises KeyError and can stall or poison-pile processing. A fallback or explicit validation/handling should be used for the new required score field.

findings.title: No coverage for eviction, large segments, or storage-format migration
findings.body: The buffer tests only exercise small segments and add end_timestamp_precise values. There are no tests for segments exceeding the new 1000-member eviction cap, behavior when existing Redis keys are still sets from the previous storage format, or correctness of eviction order/root-span handling. These are high-risk parts of the change and need tests.
